title: Arguably, the Safest Word
gist_ar: نص عن التحفّظ في اللغة: الكاتب بيهاجم استخدام الحيطة كغطاء، والموقف مش معلن.
text:
The report is, by and large, a model of caution. It concludes that the scheme
"appears to have delivered benefits to some extent", that costs were "relatively
contained", and that the approach is "arguably suitable for wider adoption,
subject to further work". Each of those is defensible. Together they are
something else.

Hedging has a legitimate function. Where evidence is genuinely tentative, "the
data tend to suggest" is more honest than a flat assertion, and a good analyst
would be right to qualify a finding that is only apparent. On the whole, our
professional literature would be improved by rather more of this and rather less
confidence.

That is not what is happening here. Notice which claims are hedged and which are
not. The benefits, which are contested, appear with every available qualifier.
The costs, which are documented and substantial, are described as contained
without reservation. Ostensibly the register is uniformly cautious; in practice
the caution is applied asymmetrically, and it is applied to precisely the
findings that would be inconvenient if stated plainly.

One might presume this is accidental. It is conceivable. Somewhat against that
reading, however, the executive summary drops the qualifiers altogether, and it
is the summary that will be quoted.

The caveat, then, is not really addressed to the reader. It is addressed to the
future — to whoever, up to a point reasonably, might later ask why the scheme was
recommended. Broadly speaking, that is what provisional language is for in
documents of this kind. It is not there to describe uncertainty. It is there to
be produced afterwards, in principle as evidence of care, and in practice as a
receipt.

questions.q: What is the writer's real objection to the report?
questions.q_ar: إيه اعتراض الكاتب الحقيقي على التقرير؟
options: It is too confident about its findings
It hedges everything equally, which is unhelpful
Its caution is applied asymmetrically, only to inconvenient findings

questions.q: What does the writer concede about hedging in general?
questions.q_ar: الكاتب بيقرّ بإيه عن اللغة المتحفّظة عمومًا؟
options: It is always evasive and has no legitimate place anywhere in professional analysis
It is legitimate where evidence is genuinely tentative
It belongs only in executive summaries

questions.q: Why does the executive summary matter to the argument?
questions.q_ar: ليه الملخص التنفيذي مهم في الحجة؟
options: It is the most cautious section
It was written by someone else
It drops the qualifiers, and it is the part that will be quoted

questions.q: What does the writer say provisional language is really for here?
questions.q_ar: الكاتب بيقول اللغة المتحفّظة موجودة ليه فعلًا هنا؟
options: To be produced later as evidence of care
To describe the genuine statistical uncertainty in the report's benefit estimates
